newsitem.title: ALBANIA: First troops arrive in rebel-held Albanian south.
newsitem.headline: First troops arrive in rebel-held Albanian south.

text.p: A small force of 25 Italian marines arrived in the rebel-held Albanian port of Vlore on Thursday, the first troops to reach the south since a multinational force landed in the chaotic Balkan state.

Witnesses said the soldiers drove from Tirana in armoured vehicles and immediately began inspecting the port area. They are part of a mission to secure humanitarian aid convoys that set up bridgeheads at Durres port and Tirana airport.
Vlore is the third key port of entry into Albania that the force of 6,000 troops from eight nations wants to secure.
A minesweeper was visible in the Adriatic outside the port.

About 300 people have been killed and more than 700 injured amid a spasm of armed violence that erupted following the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes. The uprising began in the south, which is still largely controlled by rebel councils.

In the western port of Durres, where more than 1,000 French, Italian and Spanish troops landed on Tuesday, a boat carrying 213 Italian troops arrived on Thursday. Sixty armoured vehicles and trucks rolled off the Italian naval vessel San Marco.
